knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2024_vancomycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2024_vancomycin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-023-01324-5> (open access, PMC10786964)

Zhang et al. pooled 1188 therapeutic-drug-monitoring (TDM) vancomycin
concentrations from 210 overweight and obese hospitalised patients with
varying renal function (ward and ICU) with 207 rich-sampling concentrations
from 20 morbidly obese, otherwise healthy subjects given a single dose during
bariatric surgery (the AMIGO trial, published as Smit 2020 and available here
as `Smit_2020_vancomycin`). A three-compartment model was fitted in NONMEM 7.4
(FOCE-I). Clearance increases with indexed CKD-EPI eGFR (power exponent 0.658)
and linearly with total body weight, and is 15.5% lower in ICU patients. The
authors used the model to derive AUC24 400-600 mg*h/L-targeted dosing tables
for continuous and intermittent infusion (Figures 2-5) and showed the
resulting daily AUC24 over the first week (Figures 6 and 7).

# Population

The 230 subjects (Table 1) were 140 men and 90 women, median age 70 years
(23-92), median total body weight 91.8 kg (58.6-234.6) and median BMI 30.0
kg/m^2 (25.0-65.7). The 210 TDM patients (157 ward, 53 ICU) were overweight or
obese (BMI >= 25 kg/m^2) with indexed CKD-EPI from 6.0 to 154.9 mL/min/1.73
m^2 (median 73.7); patients on renal replacement therapy were excluded. The 20
AMIGO subjects (BMI 40.8-65.7 kg/m^2, median weight 141.2 kg) all had eGFR >= 60
mL/min/1.73 m^2 and received 12.5 mg/kg (maximum 2500 mg) as a single infusion.
All subjects were treated at St. Antonius Hospital, Nieuwegein, the
Netherlands.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zhang_2024_vancomycin")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Zhang_2024_vancomycin.R`. The table below
collects them in one place.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (TVCL) | log(3.36 L/h) | Table 2, TVCL (RSE 2.60%) |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(16.7 L) | Table 2, V1 (RSE 14.0%) |
| `lq` (Q2) | log(16.1 L/h) | Table 2, Q2 (RSE 11.5%) |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(23.1 L) | Table 2, V2 (RSE 3.60%) |
| `lq2` (Q3) | log(2.44 L/h) | Table 2, Q3 (RSE 8.00%) |
| `lvp2` (V3) | log(83.0 L) | Table 2, V3 (RSE 4.50%) |
| `e_crcl_cl` (theta1) | 0.658 | Table 2, theta1 (RSE 3.10%) |
| `e_wt_cl` (theta2) | 0.0106 1/kg | Table 2, theta2 (RSE 13.8%) |
| `e_dis_critill_cl` (FICU) | 0.845 | Table 2, FICU (RSE 2.30%); footnote a: 1 if not in ICU |
| `etalcl` | 0.0730 (variance) | Table 2, IIV CL |
| `etalvc` | 0.978 (variance) | Table 2, IIV V1 |
| `addSd` | sqrt(9.32) = 3.0529 mg/L | Table 2, PA data additive error (variance) |
| `propSd_amigo` | sqrt(0.00216) = 0.046476 | Table 2, HS data proportional error (variance) |
| `addSd_amigo` | sqrt(1.10) = 1.0488 mg/L | Table 2, HS data additive error (variance) |
| CL equation | `TVCL * (CKDEPI/75)^theta1 * [1 + theta2 * (TBW - 90)] * FICU` | Table 2, first row |
| Three-compartment structure, IIV on CL and V1 only | n/a | Results, Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis |

# Typical-value clearance

The paper states that "CL was 3.36 L/h in a typical patient ... For a patient
admitted to the ICU, this value was 2.84 L/h". The model reproduces both
values at the centring values of the Table 2 equation.

```{r typical-cl, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
cl_typ <- function(CRCL, WT, ICU) {
  3.36 * (CRCL / 75)^0.658 * (1 + 0.0106 * (WT - 90)) * 0.845^ICU
}
mod <- readModelDb("Zhang_2024_vancomycin")
ref_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1:2, time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
  CRCL = 75, WT = 90, DIS_CRITILL = c(0, 1), STUDY_AMIGO = 0
)
ref_cl <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ref_ev)$cl
ref_cl
stopifnot(
  abs(ref_cl[1] - 3.36) < 1e-6,
  abs(round(ref_cl[2], 2) - 2.84) < 1e-9,
  abs(ref_cl[2] - cl_typ(75, 90, 1)) < 1e-6
)
```

# Virtual cohort

Figures 6 and 7 of the paper simulate representative virtual patients with
indexed CKD-EPI of 100, 80, 60, 40 and 20 mL/min/1.73 m^2 and total body weight
of 80, 120, 160 and 200 kg, each dosed according to the paper's dosing tables:
Figure 2 (ward, continuous infusion), Figure 3 (ward, intermittent), Figure 4
(ICU, continuous infusion) and Figure 5 (ICU, intermittent). The tables below
were transcribed by the maintainers from those figures. The paper ran 1000
simulations per patient type; 100 are used here (2000 subjects per regimen).

```{r dosing-tables}
wt_levels <- c(80, 120, 160, 200)
crcl_levels <- c(100, 80, 60, 40, 20)
wt_band_lab <- c("TBW 70-100", "TBW 100-140", "TBW 140-180", "TBW >180")
crcl_band_lab <- c("CKD >90", "CKD 70-90", "CKD 50-70", "CKD 30-50", "CKD 10-30")

# Rows: TBW 70-100, 100-140, 140-180, >180.
# Columns: CKD-EPI >90, 70-90, 50-70, 30-50, 10-30 (mL/min/1.73 m^2).
dose_tab <- function(x) matrix(x, nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)
tables <- list(
  # Continuous infusion maintenance, mg/24 h (Figures 2 and 4).
  ward_ci = dose_tab(c(
    2000, 1750, 1500, 1250, 750,
    2750, 2500, 2000, 1500, 1000,
    3750, 3250, 2750, 2000, 1250,
    4500, 4000, 3250, 2500, 1750
  )),
  icu_ci = dose_tab(c(
    1750, 1500, 1250, 1000, 750,
    2250, 2000, 1750, 1250, 1000,
    3000, 2750, 2250, 1750, 1250,
    3750, 3500, 2750, 2000, 1500
  )),
  # Intermittent: two loading doses at 0 and 12 h (mg per 2-h infusion).
  ward_ld = dose_tab(c(
    1750, 1500, 1500, 1250, 1250,
    2250, 2000, 1750, 1500, 1250,
    2500, 2250, 2250, 1750, 1500,
    3000, 2750, 2500, 2000, 1500
  )),
  icu_ld = dose_tab(c(
    2000, 1500, 1500, 1250, 1250,
    2250, 1750, 1500, 1500, 1250,
    2250, 2000, 2000, 1750, 1500,
    2750, 2250, 2250, 2000, 1500
  )),
  # Intermittent maintenance from day 2 (mg per 2-h infusion) and interval (h).
  ward_md = dose_tab(c(
    1000, 1000, 1500, 1000, 750,
    1500, 1250, 2000, 1500, 1000,
    1750, 1500, 1250, 1000, 1250,
    2250, 2000, 1750, 1250, 1750
  )),
  ward_tau = dose_tab(c(
    12, 12, 24, 24, 24,
    12, 12, 24, 24, 24,
    12, 12, 12, 12, 24,
    12, 12, 12, 12, 24
  )),
  icu_md = dose_tab(c(
    750, 750, 1250, 1000, 750,
    1000, 1000, 1750, 1250, 1000,
    1500, 1250, 1250, 1000, 1000,
    2000, 1750, 1500, 1000, 1250
  )),
  icu_tau = dose_tab(c(
    12, 12, 24, 24, 24,
    12, 12, 24, 24, 24,
    12, 12, 12, 12, 24,
    12, 12, 12, 12, 24
  ))
)
```

The continuous-infusion schedule (Figures 2 and 4) is a 1500 mg loading
infusion over 0-2 h, the maintenance infusion from 2 to 26 h, a second 750 mg
loading infusion over 26-28 h, and the maintenance infusion again from 28 h
onwards. The intermittent schedule (Figures 3 and 5) is two loading doses as
2-h infusions at 0 and 12 h, then maintenance 2-h infusions every 12 or 24 h
from 24 h.

```{r cohort}
n_per_cell <- 100L
t_end <- 168
obs_times <- seq(0, t_end, by = 1)

cell_doses <- function(setting, regimen, i, j) {
  if (regimen == "Continuous infusion") {
    md <- tables[[paste0(setting, "_ci")]][i, j]
    rate <- md / 24
    data.frame(
      time = c(0, 2, 26, 28),
      amt = c(1500, md, 750, rate * (t_end - 28)),
      rate = c(750, rate, 375, rate)
    )
  } else {
    ld <- tables[[paste0(setting, "_ld")]][i, j]
    md <- tables[[paste0(setting, "_md")]][i, j]
    tau <- tables[[paste0(setting, "_tau")]][i, j]
    md_times <- seq(24, t_end - 1, by = tau)
    data.frame(
      time = c(0, 12, md_times),
      amt = c(ld, ld, rep(md, length(md_times))),
      rate = c(ld, ld, rep(md, length(md_times))) / 2
    )
  }
}

make_cell <- function(setting, regimen, i, j, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_per_cell)
  doses <- cell_doses(setting, regimen, i, j)
  dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, doses) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L)
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0)
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    mutate(
      cmt = "central",
      WT = wt_levels[i],
      CRCL = crcl_levels[j],
      DIS_CRITILL = as.integer(setting == "icu"),
      STUDY_AMIGO = 0L,
      setting = if (setting == "icu") "ICU" else "Ward",
      regimen = regimen,
      wt_band = wt_band_lab[i],
      crcl_band = crcl_band_lab[j]
    )
}

scenarios <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  setting = c("ward", "icu"),
  regimen = c("Continuous infusion", "Intermittent"),
  i = seq_along(wt_levels),
  j = seq_along(crcl_levels)
)
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(k) {
  s <- scenarios[k, ]
  make_cell(s$setting, s$regimen, s$i, s$j, id_offset = (k - 1L) * n_per_cell)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid", "amt")])))
length(unique(events$id))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240101)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("setting", "regimen", "wt_band", "crcl_band")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

Daily AUC24 is the linear-trapezoidal area of the individual concentration
`Cc` over each 24-h day, from the hourly grid.

```{r daily-auc}
daily_auc <- sim |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(seg = (Cc + lag(Cc)) / 2 * (time - lag(time)), day = ceiling(time / 24)) |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(id, setting, regimen, wt_band, crcl_band, day) |>
  summarise(auc24 = sum(seg), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    wt_band = factor(wt_band, levels = wt_band_lab),
    crcl_band = factor(crcl_band, levels = crcl_band_lab)
  )

auc_summary <- daily_auc |>
  group_by(setting, regimen, wt_band, crcl_band, day) |>
  summarise(
    Q025 = quantile(auc24, 0.025),
    Q50 = median(auc24),
    Q975 = quantile(auc24, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-6ab, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
plot_auc <- function(which_setting, fig) {
  auc_summary |>
    filter(setting == which_setting) |>
    ggplot(aes(day, Q50)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), fill = "grey80") +
    geom_line() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(400, 600), linetype = "dashed") +
    facet_grid(crcl_band ~ regimen + wt_band) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
    labs(
      x = "Time (days)", y = "AUC24 (mg*h/L)",
      title = paste0("Figure ", fig, " (a, b): daily AUC24, ", which_setting, " patients"),
      caption = paste0("Replicates Figure ", fig, "a,b of Zhang 2024. Median and 95% prediction interval.")
    ) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))
}
plot_auc("Ward", 6)
```

```{r figure-7ab, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
plot_auc("ICU", 7)
```

```{r figure-6cd, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
plot_conc <- function(which_setting, fig) {
  sim |>
    filter(setting == which_setting) |>
    mutate(
      wt_band = factor(wt_band, levels = wt_band_lab),
      crcl_band = factor(crcl_band, levels = crcl_band_lab)
    ) |>
    group_by(regimen, wt_band, crcl_band, time) |>
    summarise(
      Q025 = quantile(Cc, 0.025), Q50 = median(Cc), Q975 = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), fill = "grey80") +
    geom_line() +
    facet_grid(crcl_band ~ regimen + wt_band) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:7) +
    labs(
      x = "Time (days)", y = "Vancomycin concentration (mg/L)",
      title = paste0("Figure ", fig, " (c, d): concentrations, ", which_setting, " patients"),
      caption = paste0("Replicates Figure ", fig, "c,d of Zhang 2024.")
    ) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))
}
plot_conc("Ward", 6)
```

```{r figure-7cd, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
plot_conc("ICU", 7)
```

The paper states that with the proposed dosing tables "the median AUC24 is
within the target of 400-600 mg*h/L, regardless of renal function, bodyweight,
and ICU admission status, even though for some ICU subgroups AUC may be
slightly above 600 mg*h/L". The check below asserts this on the centre of the
simulated distribution: the median over the 80 regimen x setting x weight x
renal-function cells of the per-cell day-7 median AUC24 lies within the
target, and every per-cell day-7 median lies within a wide envelope around it
(a mis-transcribed clearance, exponent or centring value moves whole cells by
tens of percent).

```{r auc-check}
day7 <- auc_summary |> filter(day == 7)
day1 <- auc_summary |> filter(day == 1)
summary(day7$Q50)
summary(day1$Q50)
stopifnot(
  median(day7$Q50) > 400, median(day7$Q50) < 600,
  all(day7$Q50 > 350), all(day7$Q50 < 750),
  median(day1$Q50) > 400, median(day1$Q50) < 600
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports the concentrations reached with its dosing tables "across
the entire patient population": median (interquartile range) 23.08
(19.54-27.29) mg/L for continuous infusion and a trough of 16.89 (12.65-20.50)
mg/L for intermittent dosing. PKNCA computes the day-7 (144-168 h) average
concentration and minimum concentration per simulated subject, together with
the day-1 and day-7 AUC. To keep the render fast, PKNCA uses the first 20
simulated subjects of every patient type (1600 subjects) and only the
concentrations inside the two intervals.

```{r pknca}
nca_ids <- unique(events$id[(events$id - 1L) %% n_per_cell < 20L])
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), id %in% nca_ids, time <= 24 | time >= 144) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, setting, regimen)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, setting, regimen) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, setting, regimen, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, id %in% nca_ids) |>
  select(id, time, amt, setting, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + setting + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + setting + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 144),
  end = c(24, 168),
  auclast = TRUE,
  cav = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals, options = list(auc.method = "linear", progress = FALSE)
))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
```

PKNCA's linear-trapezoidal AUC and the hand-computed daily AUC above use the
same data and the same rule, so they agree to numerical precision.

```{r pknca-vs-trapezoid}
pk_auc <- nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(day = end / 24) |>
  select(id, day, PPORRES)
both <- inner_join(pk_auc, daily_auc |> select(id, day, auc24), by = c("id", "day"))
stopifnot(nrow(both) == 2 * length(nca_ids), max(abs(both$PPORRES - both$auc24)) < 1e-6)
```

```{r nca-compare}
nca_day7 <- nca_df |> filter(start == 144)
sim_ci <- nca_day7 |>
  filter(regimen == "Continuous infusion", PPTESTCD == "cav")
sim_ii <- nca_day7 |>
  filter(regimen == "Intermittent", PPTESTCD == "cmin")
simulated <- bind_rows(sim_ci, sim_ii) |>
  select(regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cav, ~cmin,
  "Continuous infusion", 23.08, NA,
  "Intermittent", NA, 16.89
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated,
  reference = published,
  by = "regimen",
  units = c(cav = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Day-7 simulated concentration (median over ward and ICU subjects of all",
    "weight and renal-function cells) vs. the medians reported in the Results",
    "of Zhang 2024. * differs from reference by >20%."
  )
)

iqr_tab <- bind_rows(sim_ci, sim_ii) |>
  group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(PPORRES),
    q25 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(published = c("23.08 (19.54-27.29)", "16.89 (12.65-20.50)"))
iqr_tab |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Parameter" = PPTESTCD, "Simulated median" = median,
    "Simulated Q25" = q25, "Simulated Q75" = q75, "Published median (IQR)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Continuous infusion: the average concentration is AUC24 / 24, so a
# mis-transcribed clearance or dosing table moves it by tens of percent.
# The intermittent trough is a known deviation (see below) and is not gated.
stopifnot(abs(iqr_tab$median[1] / 23.08 - 1) < 0.15)
```

The continuous-infusion average concentration matches the published median.
The simulated day-7 intermittent trough (median about 13 mg/L) is about 22% below
the published 16.89 mg/L. The paper's own concentration figures agree with the
simulation rather than with that number: in Figures 6d and 7d of the paper the
median intermittent troughs fall below the 15 mg/L dashed line in many
panels, and the daily AUC24 of the same regimens (Figures 6b and 7b) is
reproduced above. The paper does not say how its pooled trough was defined
(which doses, which days, which patient types), so the difference is recorded
here as a known deviation rather than a model error.

The paper does not say which day, or which ward/ICU mix, its pooled
concentrations summarise; the comparison here uses day 7 and weights the ward
and ICU cells equally.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Centring weight of the TBW effect.** The Table 2 equation centres total
  body weight at 90 kg, `[1 + theta2 * (TBW - 90)]`, while the Results text
  describes TVCL = 3.36 L/h as the clearance of "a typical patient with a TBW
  of 100 kg". The model follows the equation. The paper's own dosing
  simulations support it: with the Figure 2 continuous-infusion doses, the
  steady-state AUC24 (dose / CL) of the representative ward patients is
  510-629 mg*h/L under 90 kg centring, matching Figure 6a, but 538-714 mg*h/L
  under 100 kg centring, which would put the 80-kg patients above the 600
  mg*h/L safety limit that Figure 6a shows them within.
- **Residual-error units.** Table 2 labels the additive residual errors "L/mg"
  and reports them as variances. They are read as variances in (mg/L)^2 and
  converted to standard deviations: 3.05 mg/L (patients) and 1.05 mg/L (AMIGO).
- **Dataset-specific residual error.** Table 2 reports an additive error for
  the hospital-patient ('PA') data and a combined additive + proportional error
  for the bariatric-surgery ('HS') data. The new indicator `STUDY_AMIGO` (1 =
  AMIGO record) selects between them. It has no effect on any structural or
  IIV parameter. Simulations of patients should set `STUDY_AMIGO = 0`.
- **ICU indicator.** ICU admission status (FICU) is encoded with the canonical
  `DIS_CRITILL` (1 = ICU), as `0.845^DIS_CRITILL` on clearance.
- **Time-varying renal function.** CKD-EPI was time-varying in the analysis
  (median 11 serum creatinine measurements per patient). It is held constant
  per virtual patient here, as in the paper's dosing simulations.
- **Simulation size and loading-dose timing.** 100 simulated subjects per
  patient type (the paper used 1000). The continuous-infusion maintenance
  infusion is paused during the 2-h day-2 loading infusion (26-28 h), which is
  how the timelines in Figures 2 and 4 draw it. The dosing tables were
  transcribed by the maintainers from Figures 2-5.
- **No errata.** No correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-10-28.
